heartbeat; null when the node's driver cannot run replicas.

maximum_active_workloads.description:

containers the node runs at once (SAKALA_MAX_ACTIVE_CONTAINERS),
for capacity-aware placement.

Optional, from nodes with the `workload-metrics` capability: one
resource sample per replica. Bounded and strict like traffic; an
item for a project or deployment the node does not serve is
well-formed and only ignored (RecordWorkloadMetricsAction).

process.description:
Additive within protocol revision 4 (ADR-022): only on worker
containers, whose samples are not project metrics.

runtime.description:
Optional and additive within protocol revision 4: where the node
is (SAKALA_AGENT_REGION) and where Sakala Edge reaches its
runtime router. An admin override on the node wins over both.
A malformed value rejects the heartbeat, like the lists above.

database.description:
Optional and additive within protocol revision 4, from nodes with
the `managed-postgres` capability (ADR-020): where attached
projects reach the PostgreSQL instance, and the size of every
database it hosts. Strict like the lists above.

available.description:
False while the agent cannot read the instance; the node then
reports `degraded` and gets no new database.

databases.description:
Only on a heartbeat right after a fresh size reading (at most
once a minute): absence means no new reading, never zero.

object_storage.description:
Optional and additive within protocol revision 4, from nodes with
the `managed-s3` capability (ADR-021): the public S3 endpoint,
its signing region, the MB the node may allocate to bucket
quotas, and the usage of every managed bucket it hosts. Strict
like the database fields: a malformed value rejects the heartbeat.

available.description:
False while the agent cannot read the instance; the node then

buckets.description:
Only on a heartbeat right after a fresh usage reading (at most
once a minute): absence means no new reading, never zero.

Stale route items: `deployment_id` is sent since v0.2.0 and is

The v0.1.0 documented payload omits this list even though the
binary sends it; accept both.

Why auto-deploy of a project is paused (`auto_deploy_pause.reason` of ProjectResource). Not stored: a rollback is the only thing that pauses it. | | |---| | `rollback`

redeploy_required.description: True while the project's serving deployment lacks the bucket variables. Deploy again to apply them.

endpoint.description: Public S3 endpoint, for example `https://s3.sakala.app`; `null` until the storage node reports it.

region.description: S3 signing region, for example `us-east-1`; `null` until the storage node reports it.

bucket.description: Bucket name on the storage node (`AWS_BUCKET`).

path_style.description: Always `true`: the endpoint serves path-style requests only.

variables.description:
Exactly the variables an attached project receives, in this order: `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3`,
`AWS_ENDPOINT`, `AWS_USE_PATH_STYLE_ENDPOINT`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_BUCKET`,
`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. `null` until the storage node reports its endpoint.

BucketKeyRotationStatus.description:
Where the newest key rotation of a managed bucket stands, read from its RotateBucketKey command. | | |---| | `pending`
Waiting for or running on the storage node. The stored secret is still the old one. | | `completed`
The node switched to the new secret: the old one no longer signs requests. | | `failed`
The node failed it definitively. The old secret still works. | | `unknown`
The node could not tell whether the new secret took effect, and the API stopped resending it after CredentialRotation::MAX_UNCERTAIN_ATTEMPTS. Neither secret is known to work; a new rotation settles it. |
BucketKeyRotationStatus.title: BucketKeyRotationStatus

status.description:
`provisioning` until the storage node creates it, then `ready`. `locked` while an admin locked it: its key is disabled, so applications cannot read or write and presigned URLs stop working. `failed` when creation failed; `deleting` while the node deletes it. A deleted bucket is gone from the API. | | |---| | `provisioning`
CreateBucket is waiting for or running on the storage node. | | `ready`
Created on the node; its key reads and writes. | | `failed`
CreateBucket failed or expired. Delete it and create another. | | `deleting`
DeleteBucket is waiting for or running on the storage node. | | `locked`
An admin locked the bucket (abuse): its key is disabled, so the application cannot read or write, and presigned URLs stop working. There is no quota lock: the node's hard quota refuses writes instead. | | `deleted`
Deleted on the node. The row is soft deleted at the same moment. |

region.description: Sakala region of the storage node, not the S3 signing region (see `connection.region`); `null` when that node has none.

quota_mb.description: Hard quota in MB the node applies, or will apply once creation finishes.

pending_quota_mb.description: The quota of a change on its way to the node, in MB; `null` when none is open.

size_bytes.description: Usage from the storage node's last report, in bytes; `null` until it reports one.

projects.description:
Projects the bucket is attached to, ordered by name. Each receives the bucket variables from its next
deployment.

connection.description:
How applications reach the bucket, without the secret: `endpoint` (the public S3 endpoint, the value of
`AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` and `AWS_ENDPOINT`), `region` (the S3 signing region, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` and
`AWS_REGION`), `bucket` (`AWS_BUCKET`), `access_key_id` (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`), and `path_style`, always
`true`. Visible to every member, viewers included: none of it is secret. `null` unless the status is
`ready` or `locked` and the node has reported its endpoint.

last_failure.description:
Set while the newest request to the storage node for this bucket failed or expired: `command` (the
agent command type), `code` (from the agent, such as `bucket_capacity_exceeded` or
`bucket_admin_unavailable`, or the control plane's `command_lease_expired`), `user_fixable` (always
`false` in this version), `summary` in Indonesian, and `failed_at`. `null` otherwise, including once a
later request succeeds or is on its way.

key_rotation.description:
The newest key rotation; `null` when the key was never rotated. `status` is `pending` while the storage
node has not reported, `completed` once only the new secret works, and `failed` when the node failed it
definitively (the old secret still works; see `last_failure`), and `unknown` when the node could not
confirm the outcome and a resend of the same secret did not complete either: neither secret is known to
work, deployments and credentials answer `409 BUCKET_KEY_ROTATING`, and a new rotation or
`buckets:reconcile` settles it. While the outcome is unconfirmed the API resends the same new
secret and the status stays `pending`. The node switches as soon
as it runs the request, so a `pending` rotation can already have cut off the old secret. The access key
ID never changes. `requested_at` is when it was asked for, `completed_at` and `failed_at` are set only
in their status. `redeploy_attached` is what the request asked for. `redeploys` is `null` until the API
has queued the redeploys after completion (and always without `redeploy_attached`), then one item per
project attached at that moment: `deployment_id` of the queued deployment (trigger
`bucket_key_rotated`), or `skipped_reason` when none was queued: `no_active_deployment`,
`requester_cannot_deploy`, `legal_acceptance_required`, `project_suspended`, `active_deployment_limit`,
`active_container_limit`, `build_rate_limit`, `repository_access_revoked`,
`database_endpoint_unavailable`, `database_not_ready`, `bucket_endpoint_unavailable`,
`bucket_not_ready`, `bucket_key_rotating`, `release_command_unsupported`, `worker_container_limit`, `worker_processes_unsupported`, or `failed`.

BucketStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a managed bucket (ADR-021). Agent command results move it; the API never assumes a node did something it did not report. | | |---| | `provisioning`
CreateBucket is waiting for or running on the storage node. | | `ready`
Created on the node; its key reads and writes. | | `failed`
CreateBucket failed or expired. Delete it and create another. | | `deleting`
DeleteBucket is waiting for or running on the storage node. | | `locked`
An admin locked the bucket (abuse): its key is disabled, so the application cannot read or write, and presigned URLs stop working. There is no quota lock: the node's hard quota refuses writes instead. | | `deleted`
Deleted on the node. The row is soft deleted at the same moment. |
BucketStatus.title: BucketStatus

current_password.description: An OAuth-only account has nothing to confirm with yet.

approved.description: The approval gate is decided by the control plane, never by the client.

release_command.description: Run once per deployment before the new version takes traffic, for example database migrations.

workspace.description: The workspace that owns the project. Null only for a project that is being purged.

redeploy_required.description: True while the project's serving deployment lacks the connection variables. Deploy again to apply them.

host.description: Host of the database node as runtime nodes reach it, on its private network; `null` until the node reports it.

url.description: `postgresql://username:password@host:port/database?sslmode=require`; `null` until the node reports its address.

sslmode.description: Always `require`: the instance only accepts TLS.

DatabaseEngine.description: Engines a managed database can run. ADR-020 starts, and for now ends, with PostgreSQL.
DatabaseEngine.title: DatabaseEngine

DatabaseExtension.description: Extensions a tenant may ask the database node to install (ADR-020). The first five are trusted by PostgreSQL; `vector` (pgvector) is not, so only the node's superuser installs it. The values are the wire names the agent accepts in InstallDatabaseExtension.
DatabaseExtension.title: DatabaseExtension

DatabasePasswordRotationStatus.description:
Where the newest password rotation of a managed database stands, read from its RotateDatabasePassword command. | | |---| | `pending`
Waiting for or running on the database node. The stored password is still the old one. | | `completed`
The node switched to the new password: the old one no longer connects. | | `failed`
The node failed it or did not finish in time. The old password still works. |
DatabasePasswordRotationStatus.title: DatabasePasswordRotationStatus

status.description:
`provisioning` until the database node creates it, then `ready`. `locked` while the workspace is at its storage quota: applications cannot connect until usage is under it again. `failed` when creation failed; `deleting` while the node drops it. A dropped database is gone from the API. | | |---| | `provisioning`
CreateDatabase is waiting for or running on the database node. | | `ready`
Created on the node and accepting connections. | | `failed`
CreateDatabase failed or expired. Nothing to connect to; delete it and create another. | | `deleting`
DropDatabase is waiting for or running on the database node. | | `deleted`
Dropped on the node. The row is soft deleted at the same moment. | | `locked`
The workspace reached its storage quota: the node turned the database's role to NOLOGIN and ended its sessions. Superuser sessions, such as the nightly backup, still connect. |

region.description: Region of the database node; `null` when that node has none. Projects attach only within one region.

size_bytes.description: Size from the database node's last report, in bytes; `null` until it reports one.

connection.description:
Where applications connect, without the password: the same host, port, database, and username attached
projects receive as `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_DATABASE`, and `DB_USERNAME`. The host is on the database
node's private network, reachable only from Sakala workloads. `null` unless the status is `ready` or
`locked` and the node has reported its address. The password and `DATABASE_URL` are only in the
credentials endpoint.

projects.description: Projects the database is attached to. Each receives the connection variables from its next deployment.

last_failure.description:
Set while the newest request to the database node for this database failed or expired: `command` (the agent
command type), `code` (from the agent, such as `database_extension_unavailable` or
`database_admin_unavailable`), `user_fixable` (`true` only when the user can fix it), `summary` in
Indonesian, and `failed_at`. `null` otherwise, including once a later request succeeds or is on its way.

password_rotation.description:
The newest password rotation; `null` when the password was never rotated. `status` is `pending` while
the database node has not reported, `completed` once the new password is the only one that connects,
and `failed` when the node failed it or did not finish in time (the old password still works; see
`last_failure`). The node switches as soon as it runs the request, so a `pending` rotation can
already have cut off the old password. `requested_at` is when it was asked for, `completed_at` and
`failed_at` are set only in their status. `redeploy_attached` is what the request asked for.
`redeploys` is `null` until the API has queued the redeploys after completion (and always without
`redeploy_attached`), then one item per project attached at that moment: `deployment_id` of the queued
deployment (trigger `database_password_rotated`), or `skipped_reason` when none was queued:
`no_active_deployment`, `requester_cannot_deploy`, `legal_acceptance_required`, `project_suspended`,
`active_deployment_limit`, `active_container_limit`, `build_rate_limit`, `repository_access_revoked`,
`database_endpoint_unavailable`, `database_not_ready`, `bucket_endpoint_unavailable`, `bucket_not_ready`, `bucket_key_rotating`, `release_command_unsupported`, `worker_container_limit`, `worker_processes_unsupported`, or `failed`.

DatabaseStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a managed database (ADR-020). Agent command results move it; the API never assumes a node did something it did not report. | | |---| | `provisioning`
CreateDatabase is waiting for or running on the database node. | | `ready`
Created on the node and accepting connections. | | `failed`
CreateDatabase failed or expired. Nothing to connect to; delete it and create another. | | `deleting`
DropDatabase is waiting for or running on the database node. | | `deleted`
Dropped on the node. The row is soft deleted at the same moment. | | `locked`
The workspace reached its storage quota: the node turned the database's role to NOLOGIN and ended its sessions. Superuser sessions, such as the nightly backup, still connect. |
DatabaseStatus.title: DatabaseStatus

DeploymentActorKind.description:
Who asked for a deployment, as `triggered_by.kind` of DeploymentResource (DeploymentTrigger::actorKind()). | | |---| | `user`
A member, by hand: deploy, redeploy, or rollback. | | `github_push`
A push to the project's branch on GitHub (auto-deploy). | | `system`
Sakala itself, for example after a database password rotation. |
DeploymentActorKind.title: DeploymentActorKind

DeploymentBuildFallbackReason.description:
Why the agent built a deployment that was planned to reuse an image, from the `reason` of its `deployment.image.reuse_skipped` event. The first four values match the agent's; `ImageUnavailable` stands for any reason this API does not know, so a newer agent never leaves the field empty. | | |---| | `image_missing`
No image of that project, commit, and deployment on the node (pruned, another node, never there). | | `image_not_owned`
The image's labels name another project or deployment. | | `image_metadata_missing`
The image has no builder label: an agent from before image reuse built it. | | `invalid_reference`
The payload's `reuse_image_from_deployment_id` was not a UUID string. | | `image_unavailable`
A reason this API does not know. |
DeploymentBuildFallbackReason.title: DeploymentBuildFallbackReason

DeploymentBuildMode.description:
How a deployment got its image. `Reused` is decided when the deployment is created (PlanDeploymentBuildAction) and stays unless the agent reports that it had to build after all (`deployment.image.reuse_skipped`), which makes it `Built`. Every deployment from before image reuse is `Built`. | | |---| | `built`
The agent builds (or built) an image from the commit. | | `reused`
The agent starts the image an earlier deployment of the project built. |
DeploymentBuildMode.title: DeploymentBuildMode

process.description:
The worker process or `job` the line came from (ADR-022); `null` for the deployment's own lines: build,
release command, and web.

triggered_by.description:
Who asked for the deployment. `user`: the member (`name` is their current name; both null once the
account is deleted). `github_push`: the pusher's GitHub name (`name` null for older deployments,
`user_id` always null). `system`: Sakala itself, both null.

rollback.description: Only for `trigger = rollback`: the deployment it went back to. Both values null once that one is deleted.

rollback_target.description:
Non-null when the project can be rolled back to this deployment now: it succeeded, is not the active one,
has a commit, ran the project's current branch, and the project is not suspended. `image_expected` is
true when the node is expected to still hold its image, so the rollback builds nothing.

generated_at.description: When the API built this table (RFC 3339); up to `SAKALA_EDGE_ROUTES_CACHE_SECONDS` old.

revision.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of `expected_minimum_routes`, `routes`, and `skipped_routes`; also the ETag.

expected_minimum_routes.description: Routes the API built; a response with fewer `routes` is truncated and must be rejected.

routes.description: One route per project that holds a workload on a node, sorted by `host`.

skipped_routes.description:
Projects that hold a workload but have no route, sorted by `host`. `reason` is
`node_without_edge_address` or `invalid_host`.

is_secret.description:
Secret unless the client says otherwise, so a forgotten flag never
makes a value readable.

project.description: The project, also when it has been deleted and waits for purge.

requested_by.description: Who asked for the deployment; null for an account deleted since.

previous_total.description: Failed deployments in the window of equal length before the range; null for `range=all`.

categories.description: Every `DeploymentFailureCategory`, most frequent first. `previous_count` is null for `range=all`.

codes.description: Every failure code seen in the range, most frequent first. `code` is null for failures recorded without one.

FeedbackStatus.description: Where an admin is with a piece of feedback. New feedback is open.
FeedbackStatus.title: FeedbackStatus

suspension.description:
Null unless the project is suspended. `reason` is what the admin wrote, as plain text;
both values are null for a suspended project without a suspend record.

databases.description:
The managed database attached to the project, as a list of at most one: a project uses one database at a
time. Only `id`, `name`, and `status`; the project detail has the connection variables.

buckets.description:
The managed bucket attached to the project, as a list of at most one: a project uses one bucket at a
time. Only `id`, `name`, and `status`; the project detail has the connection variables.

valkeys.description:
The managed Valkey store attached to the project, as a list of at most one (ADR-023). Only `id`, `name`,
and `status`. Absent while `SAKALA_VALKEY_ENABLED` is off (`valkeys.enabled` in `GET app/pilot-limits`).

workspace.description: The workspace that owns the project. Null only for a project that is being purged.

commit_message.description: First line of the commit message, as plain text: its author controls it.

The agent sends an empty JSON object; ownership and command state are
enforced by the action, not by request rules.
LeaseRepositoryCredentialRequest.title: LeaseRepositoryCredentialRequest

max_active_containers.description: Projects that serve or are being deployed at once.

max_builds_per_hour.description:
Deployments the workspace may create per rolling hour; every deployment builds. `null` follows the
global `SAKALA_PROJECT_MAX_BUILDS_PER_HOUR`.

idle_sleep_minutes.description:
Minutes without a request before a project sleeps. `0` never sleeps; `null` follows the global
`SAKALA_PROJECT_IDLE_SLEEP_MINUTES`.

max_replicas.description: Most replicas per project. `null` allows one, so replicas stay off.

default_region.description: Region the workspace's projects run in unless a project sets its own; `null` for any region.

max_databases.description:
Managed databases the workspace may hold. `null` follows the global `SAKALA_DATABASE_DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT`;
`0` allows none.

max_database_storage_mb.description:
Total size of the workspace's managed databases, in MB. `null` follows the global
`SAKALA_DATABASE_DEFAULT_MAX_STORAGE_MB`; `0` allows none.

max_buckets.description:
Managed buckets the workspace may hold. `null` follows the global `SAKALA_BUCKET_DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT`;
`0` allows none.

MB the quotas of the workspace's buckets may reserve together. `null` follows the global
`SAKALA_BUCKET_DEFAULT_MAX_STORAGE_MB`; `0` refuses new buckets and quota increases.

max_valkeys.description:
Managed Valkey stores the workspace may hold. `null` follows the global `SAKALA_VALKEY_DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT`;
`0` allows none.

MB of `maxmemory` the workspace's Valkey stores may reserve together. `null` follows the global
`SAKALA_VALKEY_DEFAULT_MAX_MEMORY_MB`; `0` refuses new stores and growth.

max_worker_containers.description:
Worker containers the workspace may run at once. `null` follows the global
`SAKALA_WORKER_DEFAULT_MAX_CONTAINERS`; `0` allows none.

max_schedules.description: Enabled schedules the workspace may hold. `null` follows the global `SAKALA_SCHEDULE_DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT`; `0` allows none.

workspace.description:
Invitations to an account's verified address, and changes to its team memberships. Invitation emails are
sent regardless, since they are the invitation itself.

email.description:
Email, independent of the in-app switch above. Only categories that can be emailed are listed:
`account_security` and `workspace` have no email preference.

deployment_success.description: Default false: a success is only worth a glance at the bell.

project_issue.description: Default true. A crash of the running app, or a push that auto-deploy skipped.

invitation_id.description: The invitation a `workspace` notification is about; open it with GET workspace-invitations/{id}.

workspace_id.description: The team a `workspace` notification is about, while the recipient still belongs to it.

email.description: Always false: email for this category is now off.

workspace_id.description: The workspace these quotas and maximums belong to.

limit_profile.description: The limit profile attached to the workspace, or null when it runs under the default for its type.

current_active_containers_count.description: Replicas of the projects that serve or are being deployed; sleeping projects do not count.

max_replicas.description: Most replicas per project, from the workspace's limit profile; 1 without one.

max_builds_per_hour.description:
Deployments the workspace may create per rolling hour, from its limit profile or the global
setting; every deployment builds. `null` means no limit.

max_databases.description: Managed databases the workspace may hold, from its limit profile or the global setting; `0` allows none.

notified; at 100 % every database of the workspace is locked. `0` allows none.

max_buckets.description: Managed buckets the workspace may hold, from its limit profile or the global setting; `0` allows none.

setting. `0` refuses new buckets and quota increases; existing buckets keep their quotas.

(ADR-022). They also count towards `max_active_containers`. `0` allows none.

max_schedules.description: Enabled schedules the workspace may hold, from its limit profile or the global setting; `0` allows none.

min_schedule_interval_minutes.description: Shortest gap between two slots of a schedule, in minutes, from its limit profile or the global setting.

max_concurrent_job_runs.description: Scheduled runs the workspace runs at once; a due run beyond that waits. `0` runs none.

max_valkeys.description: Managed Valkey stores the workspace may hold, from its limit profile or the global setting (ADR-023); `0` allows none.

current_valkeys_count.description: Managed Valkey stores that count towards `max_valkeys`: every live one except those whose creation failed.

MB of `maxmemory` the workspace's Valkey stores may reserve together, from its limit profile or the
global setting. `0` refuses new stores and growth; existing stores keep their size.

project_idle_sleep_minutes.description:
Minutes without a request before a running project of this workspace is put to sleep, from its
limit profile or the global setting. `0` means its projects never sleep.

databases.description:
Managed databases on this installation. `available` is true while at least one online database node
may receive new databases and its PostgreSQL instance last reported that it answers. False on an
installation without a database server, and while every database node is offline or its instance
is down: creating one would wait or fail. Existing databases stay listed either way.

buckets.description:
Managed S3 buckets on this installation (ADR-021). `available` is true while at least one online node
with the `managed-s3` capability may receive new buckets, has reported its object storage, and did not
report it down. `default_quota_mb` is the quota of a bucket created without `quota_mb`, before it is
capped at what the workspace has left. Absent on an API without buckets.

default_quota_mb.description:
Quota of a bucket created without `quota_mb`, in MB: `SAKALA_BUCKET_DEFAULT_QUOTA_MB`, or 256 when
unset, kept between 1 and 1048576. Never null.

workers.description:
Worker processes on this installation (ADR-022). `enabled` follows `SAKALA_WORKERS_ENABLED`; while it
is false the process endpoints answer 404 and deployments carry no workers.

schedules.description:
Scheduled jobs on this installation (ADR-022). `enabled` follows `SAKALA_SCHEDULES_ENABLED`; while it
is false the schedule endpoints answer 404 and nothing is dispatched. `default_timezone` is the
timezone of a schedule created without one, `max_timeout_seconds` the longest run timeout, and
`start_deadline_minutes` how late a slot may still start.

valkeys.description:
Managed Valkey stores on this installation (ADR-023). `enabled` follows `SAKALA_VALKEY_ENABLED`; while it
is false the Valkey endpoints answer 404 and deployments carry no store. `available` is true while it

without `maxmemory_mb`.

anyOf.description:

ProjectMetricsRange.description: Ranges of GET app/projects/{project}/metrics, each with its step and source table. The step keeps every range under about 200 points.
ProjectMetricsRange.title: ProjectMetricsRange

step_seconds.description: Width of one point: 60 for 1h, 300 for 6h, 900 for 24h, 3600 for 7d, 14400 for 30d.

series.description:
Summed across replicas. Each series has a point for every step with data, oldest first; a step without
data has no point, so consecutive `t` more than `step_seconds` apart are a gap. `t` is the start of the
step (ISO 8601, UTC). The series share the same `t` values, except that `restarts` also has a point for
a step without data in which a restart happened.

cpu_percent.description:
Percent of one CPU core, summed across replicas, so it can exceed 100. `avg` is the mean over the
step, `max` the highest per-minute (7d, 30d: per-hour) peak sum.

memory_bytes.description: Memory in bytes, summed across replicas, `avg` and `max` like `cpu_percent`.

memory_limit_bytes.description:
Summed memory limit of the replicas in the latest data of the range, in bytes. Null when there is
no data or a replica runs without a limit.

replicas.description: Replicas that reported in the step (the most in any minute, or hour for 7d and 30d).

restarts.description:
Container restarts in the step, summed across replicas. A step without data still has a point
here when a restart happened in it, so a restart is never lost to a gap.

per_replica.description:
Only with `per_replica=1`: the same series for each replica index, lowest first. Replicas of a
deployment that replaced another in the range share an index with the replica they replaced.

replicas.description: Containers of this process; `0` keeps the definition and runs nothing.

memory_mb.description: Per container, in MB; `null` follows the deployment's.

cpu_millis.description: Per container, in thousandths of a CPU; `null` follows the deployment's.

crash.description:
Set while the node reports this worker of the serving deployment as crashing (exited with a code other
than 0, or restarting over and over); `null` otherwise. A crashing worker never marks the web process
crashed. `running` true means it is up between two crashes.

redeploy_required.description: Only on the answer to a change: whether the serving deployment now differs from the project's settings.

suspension.description:
Null unless the project is suspended. `reason` is what the admin wrote, as plain text;
both values are null for a suspended project without a suspend record.

replicas.description: Containers the next deployment runs behind the node's router. Changing it applies from the next deployment.

max_replicas.description: Most replicas a project of this workspace may run, from its limit profile; 1 without one.

serving_replicas.description:
Replicas the serving deployment runs, which can differ from `replicas` until the next deployment.
Null when nothing serves, like `serving_port`.

replicas_ready.description:
Replicas of the serving deployment that pass the router's health check, from the node's heartbeat.
Null when nothing serves or the node has not reported yet.

region.description:
Region the project runs in, one of `GET app/regions`; `null` follows the workspace's default region, or
any region without one. Placement reads it only while the project has no workload on a node.

release_command.description: Run once per deployment before the new version takes traffic, for example database migrations.

auto_deploy.description: True when a push to the branch deploys now. False while paused after a rollback (see `auto_deploy_pause`).

auto_deploy_pause.description:
Non-null only while auto-deploy is paused after a rollback. `deployment_id` and `deployment_sequence` name
the rollback that paused it (null once deleted); `held_push_count` is how many pushes were recorded with
reason `auto_deploy_paused` since `paused_at`. `PATCH` with `auto_deploy` (true or false) clears it.

restart.description:
Non-null while a restart a member asked for is queued or running on the node; null once it succeeded,
failed, or expired. `requested_at` is when it was asked for.

redeploy_required.description:
True while the serving deployment was created with another deploy-relevant configuration: branch, port,
build configuration, replicas, environment variables, or the attached database or bucket (attaching,
detaching, and a rotated password or key). Changing a value back makes it false again.

variable_changes.description:
What a change to the project's own variables does to the next deployment. `requires_build` is true when any
change builds (`reason` says why); false for a plain server, where only keys starting with one of
`build_time_prefixes` (case-sensitive) or equal to one of `build_time_keys` build, and the Console shows
`build_time_prefix` for such a key. An attached database's connection variables never build. See
docs/API_CONVENTIONS.md#variabel-yang-memengaruhi-build.

databases.description:
The managed database attached to the project, as a list of at most one: a project uses one database at a
time. Its connection variables reach the next deployment; see each item's `variables`. `deploy_when_ready`
is the deployment asked for when the database was created for this project, or `null`.

buckets.description:
The managed bucket attached to the project, as a list of at most one: a project uses one bucket at a
time. Its variables reach the next deployment; see each item's `variables`.

valkeys.description:
The managed Valkey store attached to the project, as a list of at most one (ADR-023). The next
deployment joins its network and receives its variables; see each item's `variables`. Absent while
`SAKALA_VALKEY_ENABLED` is off (`valkeys.enabled` in `GET app/pilot-limits`).

workspace.description: The workspace that owns the project. Null only for a project that is being purged.

delivery_id.description: The GitHub delivery (X-GitHub-Delivery) that was skipped; one record per delivery and project.

reason.description:
Why the push did not deploy: `no_changes_in_root_directory` (it only changed other projects' folders) or
`auto_deploy_paused` (auto-deploy is paused after a rollback; the push is held).

commit_message.description: First line of the head commit's message, at most 500 characters; null without one.

root_directory.description:
The project's root directory when the push arrived, normalized (`apps/web`). Never empty for
`no_changes_in_root_directory`; `""` for `auto_deploy_paused` on a project without one.

changed_path_count.description:
Distinct files the push changed. At least 1 for `no_changes_in_root_directory`; 0 for `auto_deploy_paused`
when the payload may not list every file (a force push, a new branch, an empty commit, ...).

example_paths.description: Up to 5 of those files, sorted. For `no_changes_in_root_directory` all of them belong to other projects.

after_deployment_id.description: The project's newest deployment when the push arrived: the history shows the skip right above it.

reason.description: Why the admin is doing this. Stored in the audit event.

name.description:
Name people see, unique among the workspace's live buckets. The bucket name on the storage node is
random. Optional with `project_id`: the project's name, followed by ` 2`, ` 3`, ... when taken.

region.description:
Sakala region of the storage node, for example `jkt`. `null` (the default) uses the project's region
with `project_id`, then the workspace's default region, then any region. A bucket of any region can be
attached to any project of the workspace: the endpoint is public.

project_id.description:
A project of this workspace the caller may change, which has no bucket yet: the new bucket is attached
to it at once, while it is still `provisioning`. Another workspace's project answers `404`.

quota_mb.description:
Hard quota in MB; uploads past it are refused. Reserved from the workspace's bucket storage at once.
`null` (the default) uses `buckets.default_quota_mb` from `GET app/pilot-limits`, capped at what the
workspace has left.

deploy_when_ready.description: Not accepted in this version: a bucket never deploys its project by itself. Sending it answers `422`.

name.description:
Name people see, unique among the workspace's databases. The names on the database node are random.
Optional with `project_id`: the project's name, followed by ` 2`, ` 3`, ... when taken.

region.description:
Region of the database node, for example `jkt`. `null` (the default) uses the workspace's default region,
or any region without one; with `project_id`, the project's region first. Projects attach only to
databases of their own region.

project_id.description:
A project of this workspace the caller may change, which has no database yet: the new database is
attached to it at once, while it is still `provisioning`. Another workspace's project answers `404`.

deploy_when_ready.description:
Deploy the project as the caller once the database is ready, through the normal deployment path with
every limit. Defaults to `false`; `true` only with `project_id`.

force_build.description:
`true` always builds a fresh image. Without it, a deployment of the
live commit with no build-affecting change reuses the live image.
Defaults to `false`.

reason.description: Why the admin is doing this. Stored in the audit event.

max_active_containers.description: Projects that serve or are being deployed at once.

max_cpu_millis.description: Per project, in thousandths of a CPU.

max_builds_per_hour.description: Deployments that build an image a workspace may create in the rolling hour; redeploys that reuse the live image do not count. Null follows SAKALA_PROJECT_MAX_BUILDS_PER_HOUR (default 20).

idle_sleep_minutes.description:
Minutes without a request before a project sleeps, up to a week. `0` never puts the workspace's
projects to sleep; `null` (the default) follows `SAKALA_PROJECT_IDLE_SLEEP_MINUTES`.

max_replicas.description:
Most replicas per project, 1 to 10. `null` (the default) allows one, so replicas stay off. All replicas of a
project run on one node, which may cap them lower.

default_region.description:
Region the workspace's projects run in unless a project sets its own, for example `jkt`. `null` (the
default) places them in any region. Lowercase letters, digits, and single inner hyphens, up to 32 characters.

max_databases.description:
Managed databases the workspace may hold. `null` (the default) follows `SAKALA_DATABASE_DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT`;
`0` allows none.

max_database_storage_mb.description:
Total size of the workspace's managed databases, in MB. `null` (the default) follows
`SAKALA_DATABASE_DEFAULT_MAX_STORAGE_MB`; `0` allows none, so every database of the workspace is locked.

max_buckets.description:
Managed buckets the workspace may hold. `null` (the default) follows `SAKALA_BUCKET_DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT`;
`0` allows none.

max_bucket_storage_mb.description:
MB the quotas of the workspace's buckets may reserve together. `null` (the default) follows
`SAKALA_BUCKET_DEFAULT_MAX_STORAGE_MB`; `0` refuses new buckets and quota increases. Lowering it never
shrinks an existing bucket.

max_valkeys.description:
Managed Valkey stores the workspace may hold (ADR-023). `null` (the default) follows
`SAKALA_VALKEY_DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT`; `0` allows none.

max_valkey_memory_mb.description:
MB of `maxmemory` the workspace's Valkey stores may reserve together. `null` (the default) follows
`SAKALA_VALKEY_DEFAULT_MAX_MEMORY_MB`; `0` refuses new stores and growth. Lowering it never shrinks an
existing store.

max_worker_containers.description:
Worker containers the workspace may run at once (ADR-022). They also count against
`max_active_containers`. `null` (the default) follows `SAKALA_WORKER_DEFAULT_MAX_CONTAINERS`; `0` allows none.

max_schedules.description:
Enabled schedules the workspace may hold. `null` (the default) follows `SAKALA_SCHEDULE_DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT`;
`0` allows none.

min_schedule_interval_minutes.description:
Shortest gap between two slots of a schedule, in minutes. `null` (the default) follows
`SAKALA_SCHEDULE_DEFAULT_MIN_INTERVAL_MINUTES`.

max_concurrent_job_runs.description:
Scheduled runs the workspace runs at once; a due run beyond that waits. `null` (the default) follows
`SAKALA_SCHEDULE_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS`; `0` runs none.

Only nodes with the `release-command` capability run it.

Applies from the next deployment; `redeploy_required` turns true until then.

any region without one. Applies to the next placement on a node: a project that already runs stays on its node.

name.description: New name people see, unique among the workspace's live stores. Never changes anything on the node.

maxmemory_mb.description:
New `maxmemory` in MB: 32, 64, or 128. Needs a `ready` or `locked` store and no resize on its way.
Growth must fit the workspace's Valkey memory and the node. A persistent store refuses to shrink below
its data (`last_failure.code` `valkey_size_below_usage`); a cache store evicts keys instead.

mode.description: The mode is fixed once created. Sending it answers `422`.

password.description: Password of the `default` user (`REDIS_PASSWORD`): letters and digits only.

variables.description:
Exactly the variables an attached project receives, in this order: `REDIS_URL`, `REDIS_HOST`,
`REDIS_PORT`, `REDIS_PASSWORD`.

ValkeyMode.description:
How a managed Valkey store keeps its data (ADR-023), chosen at creation and fixed in v1. The values are the agent's `mode`, exactly. | | |---| | `cache`
No persistence, `allkeys-lru`: a full store evicts keys, a restart empties it. | | `persistent`
AOF `everysec`, `noeviction`, nightly backup: a full store refuses writes. |
ValkeyMode.title: ValkeyMode

ValkeyPasswordRotationStatus.description:
Where the newest password rotation of a managed Valkey store stands, read from its RotateValkeyPassword command. | | |---| | `pending`
Waiting for or running on the Valkey node. The stored password is still the old one. | | `completed`
The node switched to the new password and closed the old connections. | | `failed`
The node failed it definitively. The old password still works. | | `unknown`
The node could not tell whether the new password took effect (the store was down, so the change may apply when it starts), and the API stopped resending it after CredentialRotation::MAX_UNCERTAIN_ATTEMPTS. Neither password is known to work; a new rotation settles it. |
ValkeyPasswordRotationStatus.title: ValkeyPasswordRotationStatus

mode.description:
`cache`: no persistence, the least recently used keys are evicted when full, a restart empties it. `persistent`: append-only file every second, writes are refused when full, backed up nightly. Fixed. | | |---| | `cache`
No persistence, `allkeys-lru`: a full store evicts keys, a restart empties it. | | `persistent`
AOF `everysec`, `noeviction`, nightly backup: a full store refuses writes. |

status.description:
`provisioning` until the node creates it, then `ready`. `locked` while it is locked (abuse, or every attached project is suspended): applications cannot log in, the data stays. `failed` when creation failed; `deleting` while the node deletes it. A deleted store is gone from the API. | | |---| | `provisioning`
CreateValkey is waiting for or running on the Valkey node. | | `ready`
Created on the node; attached projects reach it from their next deployment. | | `failed`
CreateValkey failed or expired. Delete it and create another. | | `deleting`
DeleteValkey is waiting for or running on the Valkey node. | | `locked`
An admin locked the store (abuse, or every attached project is suspended): its `default` user is disabled, so applications cannot log in. The data stays. | | `deleted`
Deleted on the node. The row is soft deleted at the same moment. |

region.description: Sakala region of the store's node; `null` when that node has none.

maxmemory_mb.description: `maxmemory` in MB the node applies, or will apply once creation finishes.

pending_maxmemory_mb.description: The size of a resize on its way to the node, in MB; `null` when none is open.

usage.description:
The node's last reading, all `null` until it reports one: `used_memory_bytes`, `evicted_keys` (keys
evicted since the store started, cache mode), `errorstat_oom` (writes refused because the store was
full, persistent mode), `connected_clients`, `aof_last_write_status` (`ok` or `err`, persistent mode
only), `container_status` (Docker state, or `missing`), `restart_count`, and `checked_at`.

projects.description:
Projects the store is attached to, ordered by name. Each joins the store's network and receives its
variables from its next deployment.

connection.description:
How attached projects reach the store, without the password: `host` (`REDIS_HOST`, an address on the
store's private network, reachable only from attached projects) and `port` (`REDIS_PORT`, always
6379). Visible to every member. `null` until the node created the store.

last_failure.description:
Set while the newest request to the node for this store failed or expired: `command` (the agent
command type), `code` (from the agent, such as `valkey_capacity_exceeded`, `valkey_size_below_usage`,
or `valkey_in_use`, or the control plane's `command_lease_expired`), `user_fixable` (true for
`valkey_size_below_usage` and `valkey_in_use`), `summary` in Indonesian, and `failed_at`. `null`
otherwise, including once a later request succeeds or is on its way.

password_rotation.description:
The newest password rotation; `null` when it was never rotated. Same shape and meaning as
`key_rotation` of a bucket: `status` is `pending`, `completed`, `failed`, or `unknown` (the store
did not answer, so the change may apply when it starts again, and resending it did not complete:
deployments and credentials answer `409 VALKEY_PASSWORD_ROTATING` until a new rotation or
`valkeys:reconcile`). `redeploys` uses trigger `valkey_password_rotated`; `skipped_reason` adds
`valkey_not_ready`, `valkey_password_rotating`, and `valkey_node_mismatch` to the bucket list.

ValkeyStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a managed Valkey store (ADR-023). Agent command results move it; the API never assumes a node did something it did not report. | | |---| | `provisioning`
CreateValkey is waiting for or running on the Valkey node. | | `ready`
Created on the node; attached projects reach it from their next deployment. | | `failed`
CreateValkey failed or expired. Delete it and create another. | | `deleting`
DeleteValkey is waiting for or running on the Valkey node. | | `locked`
An admin locked the store (abuse, or every attached project is suspended): its `default` user is disabled, so applications cannot log in. The data stays. | | `deleted`
Deleted on the node. The row is soft deleted at the same moment. |
ValkeyStatus.title: ValkeyStatus

VariableBuildReason.description:
Why a change to a project variable makes the next deployment build instead of reusing the live image (VariableBuildPolicy). The first three are project-level: every variable counts. `BuildTimePrefix` is never a project-level reason; it names the per-variable reason of a plain server (BuildTimeVariable), so this enum lists every reason the Console can show. | | |---| | `static_site`
Served as files, without a server process: every variable is read at build. | | `prerender_framework`
A framework that can render pages at build. | | `unknown_stack`
No usable inspection, or a stack Sakala cannot classify: every variable counts, to be safe. | | `build_time_prefix`
The key is a build-time prefix or key of BuildTimeVariable. Per variable only. |
VariableBuildReason.title: VariableBuildReason
